transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15 08:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Laura (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM); Anita (Suncrest CISO), Greg (Procurement), Ravi (CTO), Lisa (Legal)

Summary: quick kickoff to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing approval path, and technical onboarding constraints (VPC, KMS, data residency). Decide pilot vs reserved capacity and next steps for legal review.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA exceptions for clinical PII, SLA uptime and latency SLOs, KMS/HSM options, SOC2/FedRAMP readiness, billing/pricing approval timeline, pilot scope (1 month, 50k tokens/day).

[00:00] Laura (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll-call then we'll jump in.
[00:08] Anita (Suncrest - CISO): Hi, Anita here. I'll start — high level we need to understand data residency and how logs are retained.
[00:15] Greg (Procurement): Greg here. Primary goal: understand acceptance path for pricing and terms so we can loop legal and finance.
[00:21] Ravi (CTO): Ravi, hello. We're mainly worried about latency for our triage assistant and also isolation — maybe dedicated.
[00:27] Laura: Great. Miguel, do you want to kick with the technical constraints?
[00:31] Miguel (Redwood SE): Sure. So quick overview — Redwood can run hosted, dedicated or private VPC. For Suncrest we usually recommend private for PHI-ish workloads but many customers use dedicated pools with Bring-Your-Own-KMS or our managed KMS. There is automatic KV cache, batching and we can tune to meet latency SLOs.
[00:53] Lisa (Legal): can you clarify, when you say managed KMS, where are keys stored and who has access to them?
[00:59] Miguel: Yeah so managed KMS = Redwood-controlled KMS in our cloud region — keys at rest are in the region and Redwood rotates per policy. BYOK path uses your KMS via a secure envelope flow. There was a small note — sorry transcription artifact — I said "envelope" flow, some people call it key wrapping.
[01:16] Anita: We prefer BYOK if possible. Our compliance team will want to keep key custody.
[01:21] Laura: Noted. On the MSA side, Lisa — any immediate dealbreakers?
[01:25] Lisa (Legal): A few asks: indemnity cap clarity, breach notification timeline tightened to 24 hours, and explicit language on subcontractors and subprocessors in the DPA. Also we have standard addendum for clinical data that we may need to attach.
[01:38] Laura: Okay, we can send redlines. Miguel — on audit logs and retention?
[01:41] Miguel: We provide audit logs for admin actions and API usage; retention configurable. Default is 90 days in hosted plan, but for Dedicated/Private we can extend. Logs contain token-level metadata but not full prompts unless specifically configured — though note some customers elect to log prompts for quality monitoring.
[02:00] Ravi: For our use case we must avoid storing raw PHI in logs unless encrypted under our keys. Could you confirm that's possible?
[02:08] Miguel: Yes — with BYOK plus log encryption we can ensure stored logs are encrypted under your keys. There's an operational caveat: streaming telemetry for console might show redacted bits unless you opt in.
[02:21] Greg: Switching to pricing — we need the list price and a committed-capacity discount path. Our procurement calendar needs a 3 week window.
[02:29] Laura: We have standard pricing for hosted per-token and per-embedding; dedicated is reserved monthly with commit tiers. We can run a pricing model for 6-month pilot vs 12-month commit.
[02:38] Greg: What's the SLA difference between hosted and dedicated?
[02:41] Miguel: Hosted has best-effort plus region failover; dedicated has an SLA for job concurrency, 99.9% uptime and latency tail guarantees depending on instance type. Real numbers depend on model and sequence length — we'll share a perf table.
[02:57] Lisa: do you offer escrow or data escrow if we terminate? We have to ensure data is retrievable and that there's a clean handoff process.
[03:05] Laura: Yes, we include exit assistance and can provide a data export. For Private deployments we also support on-prem export mechanisms. We'll include details in the MSA.
[03:13] Anita: Security questions — SOC 2 type II, pen test, vuln scanning cadence, and do you have FedRAMP status?
[03:20] Laura: Currently SOC 2 type II available, annual penetration test summary we can provide. We don't have FedRAMP yet; we do have private deployment options that help meet FedRAMP controls but cert process is customer-led.
[03:34] Miguel: Also note that for FedRAMP-type controls, the private VPC (air-gapped on-prem) path is commonly used.
[03:40] [04:05] Speaker 1 (transcription glitch): so, uh, for latency numbers, can you give an example?
[04:08] Miguel: Sure — for a 2K token request on a dedicated A100-style pool we often see median 120-160ms per token at steady state; tail latencies are higher — depends on batching. For hosted, tails can spike when load varies.
[04:29] Ravi: Is there a warmup or cache effect we should plan for on cutover?
[04:33] Miguel: There is KV cache warmup; typically first hour sees cold behavior. We recommend a brief soak period and pre-warming key prompts.
[04:43] Greg: On approval, my finance team will need line items: monthly reserved spend, overage rates, pilot discount and support entitlements.
[04:52] Laura: We'll produce a pricing workbook. Also note our billing supports PO via net-30 with standard taxonomy — we can include that in the SOW appendix.
[05:00] Lisa: On the DPA, will Redwood accept some of our clause changes around EU data transfers? Suncrest processes EU patient referrals.
[05:08] Laura: We have a standard SCC-based addendum for EU transfers; for large customers we can discuss additional clauses — we'll flag in the redline.
[05:16] Anita: One more question on monitoring — can we get token-level cost attribution per user/team? This is important for chargeback.
[05:23] Miguel: Yes — Redwood Console has token-level breakdowns and route-level dashboards. For Dedicated we can push granularity to team-level via metadata tags.
[05:33] [05:52] Greg: Who is the internal sign-off for legal? Lisa: I'll be the primary reviewer but procurement (me) and finance will sign off. Our timeline target is to have a PO in by Feb 5th if redlines are reasonable.
[05:58] Laura: Great — we will target sending the redlined MSA/DPA and SLA workbook by Monday the 19th.
[06:05] Miguel: Quick risk callout: if you pick hosted with strict DPA redlines, sometimes vendor subprocessors language causes issues — we can propose a limited subprocessor list and SOC attestation.
[06:17] Lisa: We'll need supplier attestation and a subprocessor list, yes. Also a clause on audit rights and certificate of destruction at termination.
[06:26] Miguel: For audit rights we typically provide SOC 2 report and on-site audit for enterprise private engagements; for Dedicated we support more extensive audits under NDA.
[06:36] Laura: Anything else on procurement?
[06:39] Greg: One last billing nuance — will there be any egress fees for moving logs to our archive?
[06:44] Miguel: Small egress on managed log exports; for Private we can avoid egress if it's within your VPC or on-prem. We'll add egress estimates to the workbook.
[06:55] [07:10] Ravi: Technical acceptance — we want a short runbook for the pilot: test corpus, latency tests, quality gates, and rollback plan.
[07:17] Miguel: We'll put together an acceptance plan: baseline perf, smoke tests, end-to-end with simulated traffic, and a fallback to a smaller model if QoS degrades.
[07:26] Laura: OK, let's run through explicit next steps and owners.
[07:29] Laura (Redwood AE): Next steps recap — Redwood will: 1) send MSA/DPA redline + SLA workbook + SOC2/pentest docs (owner: Laura; due: 2026-01-19). 2) Miguel sends dedicated vs hosted perf delta doc + pilot acceptance runbook (due: 2026-01-20).
[07:46] Greg (Suncrest): My side: procurement sends preferred PO terms and questionnaire answers (owner: Greg; due: 2026-01-22). Lisa will review redlines and provide legal feedback by 2026-01-26.
[07:56] Anita: I'll confirm data residency requirement (USA-only or multi-region) and KMS custody preference by end of week (owner: Anita; due: 2026-01-18).
[08:05] Laura: Perfect. Scorecard — planned 1 month pilot, 50k tokens/day, dedicated pool consideration pending budget.
[08:13] [08:20] Speaker 2 (misc): small cross talk about calendar invites and follow-ups.
[08:25] Laura: That's all from us — we'll follow up with the doc bundle. Thanks everyone.
[08:29] Lisa: Thanks.
[08:30] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: there are a few transcription glitches around technical terms (KV cache, KMS envelope) and occasional speaker mis-labeling.
